review_type: Drafting-assistant bilingual self-reread; not human or independent scholarly review

rows.rationale: Preserves real authority and the command Paul could issue.
rows.before: Therefore, although I have great boldness in Christ to command you to do what is fitting,
rows.after: Therefore, though in Christ I have great boldness to command you to do what is fitting,
rows.tsw_comparator: Accordingly, though I am bold enough in Christ to command you to do what is required,
rows.exact_source_record: Διό, πολλὴν ἐν Χριστῷ παρρησίαν ἔχων ἐπιτάσσειν σοι τὸ ἀνῆκον,

rows.rationale: Keeps appeal, age claim and imprisonment as persuasive pressure.
rows.before: because of love I prefer to appeal to you—being such a person as Paul, an old man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
rows.after: I prefer to appeal to you on the basis of love—being who I am, Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
rows.tsw_comparator: yet for love’s sake I prefer to appeal to you—I, Paul, an old man and now a prisoner also for Christ Jesus—
rows.exact_source_record: διὰ τὴν ἀγάπην μᾶλλον παρακαλῶ, τοιοῦτος ὢν ὡς Παῦλος πρεσβύτης νυνὶ δὲ καὶ δέσμιος ⸂Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ⸃—

rows.rationale: Names Onesimus and keeps spiritual parenthood and prison context.
rows.before: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became in my chains.
rows.after: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became while in chains.
rows.tsw_comparator: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became in my imprisonment.
rows.exact_source_record: παρακαλῶ σε περὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ τέκνου, ὃν ἐγέννησα ἐν τοῖς ⸀δεσμοῖς Ὀνήσιμον,

rows.before: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
rows.after: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
rows.tsw_comparator: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he is indeed useful to you and to me.
rows.exact_source_record: τόν ποτέ σοι ἄχρηστον νυνὶ ⸀δὲ σοὶ καὶ ἐμοὶ εὔχρηστον,

rows.rationale: Keeps involuntary return and intense bodily affection.
rows.before: I am sending him back to you—him, that is, my own heart.
rows.after: I am sending him back to you—him, that is, my own heart.
rows.tsw_comparator: I am sending him back to you, sending my very heart.
rows.exact_source_record: ὃν ἀνέπεμψά ⸂σοι αὐτόν, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τὰ ἐμὰ σπλάγχνα⸃·

rows.rationale: Retains Paul's desire, expected service and incarceration.
rows.before: I wanted to keep him with me so that he might serve me on your behalf in my chains for the good news.
rows.after: I wanted to keep him with me, so that he might serve me on your behalf while I am in chains for the good news.
rows.tsw_comparator: I would have been glad to keep him with me, in order that he might serve me on your behalf during my imprisonment for the gospel,
rows.exact_source_record: ὃν ἐγὼ ἐβουλόμην πρὸς ἐμαυτὸν κατέχειν, ἵνα ὑπὲρ σοῦ ⸂μοι διακονῇ⸃ ἐν τοῖς δεσμοῖς τοῦ εὐαγγελίου,

rows.rationale: Keeps consent and coercion contrast within an unequal relationship.
rows.before: But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good deed might not be by compulsion but willingly.
rows.after: But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your good deed would not be forced but voluntary.
rows.tsw_comparator: but I preferred to do nothing without your consent, in order that your goodness might not be by compulsion but of your own accord.
rows.exact_source_record: χωρὶς δὲ τῆς σῆς γνώμης οὐδὲν ἠθέλησα ποιῆσαι, ἵνα μὴ ὡς κατὰ ἀνάγκην τὸ ἀγαθόν σου ᾖ ἀλλὰ κατὰ ἑκούσιον·

rows.rationale: Preserves cautious perhaps and passive separation.
rows.before: Perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while: so that you might have him back forever,
rows.after: Perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while, so that you might have him back forever,
rows.tsw_comparator: For this perhaps is why he was parted from you for a while, that you might have him back forever,
rows.exact_source_record: τάχα γὰρ διὰ τοῦτο ἐχωρίσθη πρὸς ὥραν ἵνα αἰώνιον αὐτὸν ἀπέχῃς,

rows.rationale: Names enslaved status and the requested transformed relationship without inventing manumission.
rows.before: no longer as a slave but more than a slave—a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
rows.after: no longer merely as a slave but more than a slave—as a beloved brother, especially to me, and how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
rows.tsw_comparator: no longer as a slave but more than a slave, as a beloved brother—especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
rows.exact_source_record: οὐκέτι ὡς δοῦλον ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ δοῦλον, ἀδελφὸν ἀγαπητόν, μάλιστα ἐμοί, πόσῳ δὲ μᾶλλον σοὶ καὶ ἐν σαρκὶ καὶ ἐν κυρίῳ.

rows.rationale: Keeps partnership as the appeal's direct basis.
rows.before: Therefore, if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would me.
rows.after: So if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
rows.tsw_comparator: So if you consider me your partner, receive him as you would receive me.
rows.exact_source_record: Εἰ οὖν με ἔχεις κοινωνόν, προσλαβοῦ αὐτὸν ὡς ἐμέ.

rows.rationale: Preserves possible harm, debt and Paul's assumption of liability.
rows.before: If he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge that to me.
rows.after: If he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to me.
rows.tsw_comparator: If he has wronged you at all, or owes you anything, charge that to my account.
rows.exact_source_record: εἰ δέ τι ἠδίκησέν σε ἢ ὀφείλει, τοῦτο ἐμοὶ ⸀ἐλλόγα·

rows.rationale: Keeps autograph promise and the explicit counter-debt pressure.
rows.before: I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me even your own self.
rows.after: I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me your very self.
rows.tsw_comparator: I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—to say nothing of your owing me even your own self.
rows.exact_source_record: ἐγὼ Παῦλος ἔγραψα τῇ ἐμῇ χειρί, ἐγὼ ἀποτίσω· ἵνα μὴ λέγω σοι ὅτι καὶ σεαυτόν μοι προσοφείλεις.

rows.rationale: Preserves Onesimus-related wordplay and the repeated heart-refreshing request.
rows.before: Yes, brother, let me have this benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.
rows.after: Yes, brother, let me benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
rows.tsw_comparator: Yes, brother, I want some benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.
rows.exact_source_record: ναί, ἀδελφέ, ἐγώ σου ὀναίμην ἐν κυρίῳ· ἀνάπαυσόν μου τὰ σπλάγχνα ἐν ⸀Χριστῷ.

rows.rationale: Keeps expectation, obedience language and open-ended further action.
rows.before: Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
rows.after: Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
rows.tsw_comparator: Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.
rows.exact_source_record: πεποιθὼς τῇ ὑπακοῇ σου ἔγραψά σοι, εἰδὼς ὅτι καὶ ὑπὲρ ⸀ἃ λέγω ποιήσεις.

rows.rationale: Retains prospective visit and added social accountability.
rows.before: At the same time, prepare a guest room for me, because I hope that through your prayers I will be graciously given back to you.
rows.after: At the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be restored to you.
rows.tsw_comparator: At the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I am hoping that through your prayers I will be graciously given to you.
rows.exact_source_record: ἅμα δὲ καὶ ἑτοίμαζέ μοι ξενίαν, ἐλπίζω γὰρ ὅτι διὰ τῶν προσευχῶν ὑμῶν χαρισθήσομαι ὑμῖν.
